title: DIRT video: @Joe Weinberg #broadway #offbroadway #musicaltheatre #pla...
transcript: you are running out of time to see some of the best theatre in New York so here is a time-sensitive round up of theatre closing before the end of February most of these are shows that I either (a) saw and recommend or (b) shows that I'm planning to see before they close. although I'm gonna include two shows that I unfortunately don't think I'm gonna catch but I've heard good things about them: the first of which is this production of King Lear at La Mama with a great cast and the Honey Trap at Irish Rep which I've heard has a lot of exciting twists and turns. closing pretty soon on February 8th is a production with a lot of positive buzz this riveting and cleverly reimagined telling of Oedipus. we have several shows closing February 15th including Watch Me Walk by Anne Gridley which is like part autobiography, part theatrical variety show finding a lot of creative ways to explore her experiences with disability from different angles. we have Dirt, this interactive theatre piece that's also kind of a game and it imagines what if the East River suddenly disappeared one day if you wanna hear more about this one I made a video which I'll link in the caption but it's one of my favorite theatrical experiences of the season so far. we have the Encores revival of the musical High Spirits based on the Noel Coward play Blithe Spirit and this one stars real life married couple Philippa Soo and Steven Pasquale alongside Tony winners Katrina Lenk and Andrea Martin next we have the Broadway production of Marjorie Prime a Pulitzer-finalist play with a fantastic cast and a chilling SCI fi premise I will say it took me a while to get into this one but by the end it it's a pretty big punch and leaves a lot to chew on afterward closing the following week is Gooey's Toxic Aquatic Adventure which appears to be a post apocalyptic mermaid puppet musical I have the description up here because I don't think I can do justice to it. next I wanna give a shout out to Hell's Kitchen which is ending its respectable two year run on Broadway I won't deny that the book is flawed but when I saw it at the public I really couldn't help but get swept up in the energy and vibes of it all This week I'm finally getting around to seeing Dirty Books thanks to its multiple extensions. I believe it's an interactive theatre piece about 1960s anti obscenity and censorship laws and I've heard good things about it! playing a short run at St. Ann’s Warehouse is Hate Radio which places you in the room depicting a real time radio broadcast during a conflict in Rwanda. for the purposes of this list I'm also including three shows that end on March 1st including Edward another interactive show where the audience chooses the order of these episodic stories from one man's life and it's performed in a series of bookstores around the city. it is sold out but keep your eyes open because this is already their 3rd run in New York so maybe it'll come back. then we have this production of Coriolanus one of the less frequently produced Shakespeare plays and this production incorporates some sort of examination of like video game violence or screen violence or something. and finally the Dinosaurs where we see a series of meetings between a group of women but it kind of blurs time where like we're following them over the course of multiple centuries or millennia. so that's what I have for you but feel free to let me know in the comments if I missed anything big!
classificationReason: Explicitly a time-sensitive roundup of multiple shows closing before end of February (King Lear, Honey Trap, Oedipus, Watch Me Walk, Dirt, and more — well over 3 shows) with no single primary focus.
